BAS3-01.note: No reordering keeps the object-control frame.

BAS3-02.note: Marginal: 'For the next bus the manager told us to wait' (topicalized PP, stilted without comma).

BAS3-04.note: Only a yes/no question 'Had I forgotten to lock the back door', which needs a question mark.

alternatives: he borrowed | the book | He | promised | to return
BAS3-05.note: Swap the clauses: 'He borrowed the book he promised to return.' Fully grammatical and natural, with a different meaning. The capitalised 'He' chip becomes the relative-clause subject and the lowercase 'he borrowed' chip opens the sentence (case ignored).

BAS3-08.note: Marginal: 'Is it important to read the instructions carefully' (question, needs a ?).

BAS3-09.note: Marginal: question 'Is she afraid of losing her job'.

BAS3-10.note: Marginal: question 'Are we looking forward to seeing you' (odd).

BAS3-14.note: 'Having broken the window he admitted' needs a comma and changes the meaning. Rejected.

BAS3-17.note: 'The old car expected nobody to start so easily' is grammatical but nonsensical. Rejected.

BAS3-20.note: Marginal: 'Nothing but old photographs the box contained' (archaic topicalization).

alternatives: Everyone | enjoyed | the concert | except | my brother
BAS3-21.note: The except-phrase can move to the end: 'Everyone enjoyed the concert except my brother.' Fully natural, arguably more common than the key. 'Except my brother everyone enjoyed the concert' would need a comma, so it is marginal.

BAS3-22.note: Marginal: question 'Has she been working on the same project'.

BAS3-23.note: Marginal: 'How late it was I didn't realize' (topicalization, stilted).

BAS3-24.note: Marginal: 'Why I had left he wanted to know' (topicalization).

BAS3-25.note: Marginal: question 'Is this the first time I have flown alone'.

BAS3-27.note: Marginal: question 'Is the old museum well worth a visit'.

BAS3-28.note: Marginal: exclamatory or question inversion 'Was I surprised to see so many people' (natural spoken exclamation, but needs ! or ?).

BAS3-29.note: Marginal: question 'Had we run out of printer paper'.

BAS3-33.note: Marginal: question 'Is there no point in arguing'.

alternatives: she had trained for | the race | She | managed | to finish
BAS3-34.note: Swap the clauses: 'She had trained for the race she managed to finish.' Grammatical and natural, with a different meaning. Same mechanism as BAS3-05: a lowercase-subject clause chip plus a separate capitalised subject chip.

BAS3-35.note: Marginal: 'In English our teacher strongly recommends reading the novel' (fronted PP, needs a comma to read well).

BAS3-37.note: Marginal: question 'Was it kind of you to help'.

BAS3-39.note: Marginal: question 'Is he likely to arrive late'.

BAS3-42.note: Marginal, as questions only: 'Who was the only one she noticed' and 'Was she the only one who noticed'. Both are grammatical wh- or yes/no questions but need a question mark.

BAS3-43.note: Marginal: question 'Were the students asked to hand in their essays'.

BAS3-48.note: Marginal: question 'Is it no use complaining about it'.
